[[Pro-Europeanism]] | position = [[Centre-left politics|Centre-left]] | continental = [[Unified European Left Group]]{{Cite web |title=STEPHENSON, PATRICIA |url=https://pace.coe.int/en/members/9105/stephenson}} | colours = {{colour box|{{party color|Social Democrats (Ireland)}}}} Purple | seats1_title = [[Dáil Éireann]] | seats1 = {{Political party data|seat composition bar|ms-lower-house}} | seats2_title = [[Seanad Éireann]] | seats2 = {{Political party data|seat composition bar|ms-upper-house}} | seats3_title = [[Local government in the Republic of Ireland|Local government]] | seats3 = {{composition bar|31|949|hex={{party color|Social Democrats (Ireland)}}}} | website = {{Political party data|website}} | country = the Republic of Ireland }} The '''Social Democrats''' ({{Langx|ga|Na Daonlathaithe Sóisialta}}){{Cite web|title=Tionóil fómhair ag na Daonlathaithe Sóisialta agus an Lucht Oibre|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/nuacht/2023/0914/1405256-tionoil-fomhair-ag-na-daonlathaithe-soisialta-agus-an-lucht-oibre/|access-date=9 July 2024|website=[[RTÉ]]|language=Irish|date=14 September 2023|first=Irene|last=Ní Nualláin}} are a [[Social democracy|social democratic]] [[List of political parties in the Republic of Ireland|political party in Ireland]]. Led by [[Holly Cairns]] since March 2023, the party was launched on 15 July 2015 by three [[Independent politician (Ireland)|independent]] [[Teachta Dála|TDs]]: [[Catherine Murphy (politician)|Catherine Murphy]], [[Róisín Shortall]], and [[Stephen Donnelly]]. It promotes the [[Nordic model]] of political economy,{{cite news |first=Catherine |last=Murphy |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/we-have-a-swede-dream-for-the-future-of-ireland-xn0p2bqsc5n |title=We have a Swede dream for the future of Ireland |publisher=The Sunday Times |date=2015-07-19 |access-date=2018-04-09 |archive-date=5 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805221518/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/we-have-a-swede-dream-for-the-future-of-ireland-xn0p2bqsc5n |url-status=live}} [[pro-European]] views,{{cite web|url=https://europeelects.eu/european-union/ireland/|title=Ireland|website=[[Europe Elects]]|access-date=1 April 2019|archive-date=1 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401163146/https://europeelects.eu/european-union/ireland/|url-status=live}} and implementing [[Sláintecare]], a plan to reform the [[Healthcare in the Republic of Ireland|Irish healthcare system]]. ==History== === 2015–2019: Foundation and early elections === The Social Democrats was established with a co-leadership arrangement between its three founding members. [[Róisín Shortall]] is a former [[Labour Party (Ireland)|Labour Party]] [[Teachta Dála|TD]] and former [[Minister of State at the Department of Health]]. She resigned from the role and from Labour in September 2012, citing lack of support and the lack of an explanation from then-[[Minister for Health (Ireland)|Minister for Health]] [[James Reilly (Irish politician)|James Reilly]] concerning his controversial decision to locate a new [[Primary care|primary care centre]] in his own constituency.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/news/2012/0926/reilly-and-shortall-meeting-tense-and-difficult.html|title=Roisin Shortall resigns as junior health minister|work=[[RTÉ News]]|date=26 September 2012|access-date=26 September 2012|archive-date=28 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928232130/http://www.rte.ie/news/2012/0926/reilly-and-shortall-meeting-tense-and-difficult.html|url-status=live}} [[Catherine Murphy (politician)|Catherine Murphy]] was successively a member of the [[Workers' Party (Ireland)|Workers' Party]], [[Democratic Left (Ireland)|Democratic Left]] and the Labour Party before being elected as an independent TD in 2005. [[Stephen Donnelly]] first entered politics as an independent TD in the [[2011 Irish general election|2011 general election]], having previously worked as a consultant for [[McKinsey and Company]]. Both Murphy and Donnelly were members of the [[Technical group|Technical Group]] in the 31st Dáil, with Murphy having served as its [[Chief Whip]]. The party ran fourteen candidates in the [[2016 Irish general election|2016 general election]], including its three incumbent TDs, former Labour Party [[Seanad Éireann|Senator]] [[James Heffernan (Irish politician)|James Heffernan]], and county councillors [[Gary Gannon]] and [[Cian O'Callaghan]].{{cite news|url=http://www.breakingnews.ie/ireland/social-democrats-reveal-five-election-candidates-694303.html|title=Social Democrats reveal five election candidates|work=BreakingNews.ie|date=4 August 2015|access-date=4 September 2015|archive-date=5 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905171755/http://www.breakingnews.ie/ireland/social-democrats-reveal-five-election-candidates-694303.html|url-status=live}} Their three incumbent TDs were re-elected, but none of their other candidates were elected. In May 2016, the party formed a technical group within the Dáil with the [[Green Party (Ireland)|Green Party]].{{Cite web|title=Social Democrats and Green Party form Dáil technical group|url=http://utv.ie/News/2016/05/30/Social-Democrats-and-Green-Party-form-Dail-technical-group-59759|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630044306/http://utv.ie/News/2016/05/30/Social-Democrats-and-Green-Party-form-Dail-technical-group-59759|archive-date=30 June 2016}}{{cite web |author=Social Democrats |url=https://twitter.com/SocDems/status/737294710419644416 |title=We can confirm we have entered into a Technical Arrangement (Tech Group) with @greenparty_ie for this Dáil. |publisher=Twitter.com |date=2016-05-30 |access-date=2018-04-09 |archive-date=24 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190524202226/https://twitter.com/SocDems/status/737294710419644416 |url-status=live}} On 5 September 2016, Stephen Donnelly resigned as joint leader and left the party, stating that he was doing so "with great sadness, having vested so much together with my parliamentary colleagues, Catherine and Roisin, a small core team and many volunteers across the country, into the establishment of the Social Democrats over the last 20 months", but referring to his relationship with his fellow leaders, that "some partnerships simply don't work".{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/politics/stephen-donnelly-quits-social-democrats-in-major-blow-for-party-35022379.html|title='Some partnerships simply don't work' - Stephen Donnelly quits Social Democrats in major blow for party|date=5 September 2016}} On 2 February 2017, he joined [[Fianna Fáil]].{{cite web |first=Pat |last=Leahy |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/wicklow-td-stephen-donnelly-to-join-fianna-f%C3%A1il-party-says-1.2960715 |title=Wicklow TD Stephen Donnelly to join Fianna Fáil, party says |publisher=Irishtimes.com |date=2017-02-02 |access-date=2018-04-09 |archive-date=14 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914173647/https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/wicklow-td-stephen-donnelly-to-join-fianna-f%C3%A1il-party-says-1.2960715 |url-status=live}} === 2019 local and European elections === The Social Democrats contested their first [[2019 European Parliament election in Ireland|European Parliament elections]] in May 2019, with councillor [[Gary Gannon]] running for election in the [[Dublin (European Parliament constituency)|Dublin]] constituency.{{Cite web |date=2019-03-19 |title=Cllr Gary Gannon to contest Dublin seat in Euro Elections |url=https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/2019/03/19/cllr-gary-gannon-to-contest-dublin-seat-in-euro-elections/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423125716/https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/2019/03/19/cllr-gary-gannon-to-contest-dublin-seat-in-euro-elections/ |archive-date=23 April 2019 |access-date=2019-04-24 |website=Social Democrats |language=en-US}} Gannon received 5.6% of the first-preference votes, finishing 6th out of 19 candidates in the first count. He was eliminated on the 14th count. The party did not contest the other Irish constituencies of [[Midlands–North-West]] or [[South (European Parliament constituency)|South]] at this election. The party also contested their first local elections in May 2019. The Social Democrats put forward 58 candidates for seats on local councils. 55% of the candidates were women, making it the second highest percentage of female candidates put forward among all political parties.{{Cite web |last=Kavanagh |first=Adrian |date=2018-10-16 |title=Female candidates contesting the 2019 Local Elections |url=https://adriankavanaghelections.org/2018/10/16/female-candidates-contesting-the-2019-local-elections/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423125716/https://adriankavanaghelections.org/2018/10/16/female-candidates-contesting-the-2019-local-elections/ |archive-date=23 April 2019 |access-date=2019-04-24 |website=Irish Elections: Geography, Facts and Analyses |language=en}} 19 of the 58 candidates were elected, more than trebling the party's representation in local government.{{cite news |last=Bray |first=Jennifer |date=26 May 2019 |title=Social Democrats 'reasonably happy' with the party's performance |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/social-democrats-reasonably-happy-with-the-party-s-performance-1.3905203 |access-date=29 May 2019}} [[Ellie Kisyombe]], a [[Malawi]]-born asylum seeker running for the Social Democrats in Dublin's North Inner City LEA, was retained after a review of inconsistencies in her account of her asylum history and time in [[direct provision]]; following this, three members of the party's National Executive resigned.{{cite news |last1=Bray |first1=Jennifer |date=4 May 2019 |title=Ellie Kisyombe to run in elections after correcting backstory, party says |language=en |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/local-elections/ellie-kisyombe-to-run-in-elections-after-correcting-backstory-party-says-1.3881481 |url-status=live |access-date=22 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210120044927/https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/local-elections/ellie-kisyombe-to-run-in-elections-after-correcting-backstory-party-says-1.3881481 |archive-date=20 January 2021}} === 2019 by-elections and the 2020 general election === In November 2019, the party contested 3 of the 4 by-elections caused by the election of Irish TDs to the European Parliament, but did not win any seats, with their candidates all receiving between 2.5% and 4.4% of the vote. In the [[2020 Irish general election|2020 general election]], the party ran 20 candidates in 20 constituencies, and increased their seats to six, despite a small fall in the number of first preference votes received. Murphy and Shortall were re-elected in their constituencies, and were joined by [[Holly Cairns]] in [[Cork South-West]], [[Gary Gannon]] in [[Dublin Central]], [[Cian O'Callaghan]] in [[Dublin Bay North]] and [[Jennifer Whitmore]] in [[Wicklow (Dáil constituency)|Wicklow]]. The Social Democrats finished level on seats with the [[Labour Party (Ireland)|Labour Party]] and exceeded the seats of other left-leaning parties [[Solidarity–People Before Profit]] and [[Independents 4 Change]].{{cite web |title=General Election candidates |url=https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/GE-Candidates/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191018210015/https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/GE-Candidates/ |archive-date=18 October 2019 |access-date=21 January 2020 |publisher=Social Democrats}} ===Holly down as co-leaders of the Social Democrats.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/politics/2023/0222/1358185-social-democrats/|title=Shortall and Murphy to stand down as co-leaders of Social and she was announced as the new leader on 1 March.{{cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2023/0226/1358983-social-democrats-leadership-latest/|title=Holly Cairns puts herself forward for Irish local elections|June 2024 local elections]], the Social Democrats ran 78 candidates, with 35 elected, including 10 on [[Dublin City Council]], where they became the second largest party.{{cite web|url=https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/cairns-hails-impressive-local-election-results-for-soc-dems/|title=Cairns hails impressive local election results for Soc Dems|publisher=Social Democrats|date=10 June 2024|access-date=12 June 2024}} For the [[2024 European Parliament election in Ireland|2024 European elections in Ireland]], the party ran three candidates, one in each of the Irish [[European Parliament constituencies in the Republic of Ireland|constituencies]]. While the Social Democrats' first preference vote share increased to 2.95%, none of their candidates were elected.{{Cite web |title=RTÉ Elections 2024, European Elections |url=https://www.rte.ie/news/elections-2024/results/#/european/national/ |access-date=June 19, 2024 |website=RTÉ News}} At the [[2024 Irish general election|2024 general election]] in November, the party almost doubled its number of TDs, going from 6 to 11, tying with Labour to become the fourth-largest party in Ireland.{{cite news |date=3 December 2024 |title=General Election 2024 as it happened: The campaign, the count and the aftermath |url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/elections-2024/general-election-2024-as-it-happened-the-campaign-the-count-and-the-aftermath/a1651848310.html |work=[[Irish Independent]] |location= |access-date=3 December 2024}} The party also gained its first Senator in [[Patricia Stephenson]] at the [[2025 Seanad election]]. However, the party lost a TD at the same time following the indefinite suspension of [[Eoin Hayes]].{{cite news |last=Pepper |first=Diarmuid |date=11 February 2025 |title=Eoin Hayes' suspension from Social Democrats endorsed by party's national executive |url=https://www.thejournal.ie/eoin-hayes-suspension-from-social-democrats-endorsed-national-executive-6619699-Feb2025/ |work=[[TheJournal.ie]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=11 February 2025}} In July 2025 Hayes was readmitted to the parliamentary party.{{Cite web |last=Horgan-Jones |first=Jack |title=Eoin Hayes readmittance by Social Democrats a bid to put an end to difficult question for party |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/politics/2025/07/31/eoin-hayes-readmittance-by-social-democrats-a-bid-to-put-an-end-to-difficult-question-for-party/ |access-date=2025-08-05 |website=The Irish Times |language=en}} Shortly after Hayes' readmission, Galway city councillor Eibhlín Seoighthe resigned from the party.{{Cite web |last=O’Halloran |first=Jack Horgan-JonesMarie |title=Galway city councillor resigns from Social Democrats |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/politics/2025/07/31/galway-city-councillor-resigns-from-social-democrats/ |access-date=2025-08-05 |website=The Irish Times |language=en}} ==== 2025 presidential election ==== The party jointly nominated [[Catherine Connolly]] in the [[2025 Irish presidential election]] as part of a broad left-wing alliance. They first announced their intention to support Connolly on 11 July 2025, alongside [[People Before Profit]], [[100% Redress]] and several [[Independent politician (Ireland)|independent politicians]]. Party leader, [[Holly Cairns]] stated that these were the party's red-lines.{{Cite web |date=2024-11-12 |title=Disability ministry and affordable homes among Social Democrats' red lines |url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/general-election-2024/disability-ministry-and-affordable-homes-among-social-democrats-red-lines-1694791.html |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=BreakingNews.ie |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=McNally |first=Tadgh |date=2024-11-12 |title=Social Democrats say 50,000 affordable homes is their 'red line' for government |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/politics/arid-41515496.html |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=Irish Examiner |language=en}} * Build 50,000 affordable purchase homes. * Fully implement [[Sláintecare]]. * Agree a plan to reach Irish climate targets and avoid €8 billion in fines. * Appoint a full cabinet [[Minister (government)|Minister]] for Disability. * Build high quality public childcare. === Healthcare === One of the party's core policies is ''[[Sláintecare]]'', an Irish national health service proposal. ''Sláintecare'' is a fully costed plan for a universal, single-tier public health service that would join up health and social care in Ireland and be free at the point of use.{{cite web |url= https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/our-policies/health/ |title= Health |website= socialdemocrats.ie |publisher= Social Democrats |access-date= 14 December 2023}} ''Sláintecare'' was developed as the result of a cross-Party Oireachtas Committee chaired by the Social Democrats' [[Róisín Shortall]], which sought to examine the issue of healthcare in Ireland. The party's ''Sláintecare'' policy plan also includes (but is not limited to): a legal entitlement to homecare packages for older people, significantly reducing [[Prescription charges#Ireland|prescription charges]] and lowering costs for medicines, providing access to basic procedures at a local level, and improved funding for mental health, including counselling, community programmes, and adult mental health teams.[https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/what-we-stand-for/building-an-irish-health-service/ Our plan for healthcare] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903013309/https://www.socialdemocrats.ie/what-we-stand-for/building-an-irish-health-service/ |date=3 September 2018}}. extract: The Social Democrats (Irish: Na Daonlathaithe Sóisialta) are a social democratic political party in Ireland. Led by Holly Cairns since March 2023, the party was launched on 15 July 2015 by three independent TDs: Catherine Murphy, Róisín Shortall, and Stephen Donnelly. It promotes the Nordic model of political economy, pro-European views, and implementing Sláintecare, a plan to reform the Irish healthcare system.
